market_context: The post-open tape shows a sharp rotation away from AI/semiconductors: QQQ is down 1.36% while DIA and IWM are positive, with NVDA down 5.41% after Monday's outsized rally. AP reported tech led the early decline, while November Conference Board consumer confidence printed 92.25 versus 91.7 previously; the slightly firmer macro reading and 4.91% 10-year yield keep rate-sensitive growth under pressure. (apnews.com)

predictions.reasoning: SPY is holding near the top of its early range despite QQQ's larger decline, suggesting Dow and small-cap strength is cushioning the index rather than producing broad risk-on participation. Elevated VIX at 28 and persistent semiconductor selling should leave the S&P modestly lower from the 10:00 AM baseline into the close.

The Nasdaq-100 is materially underperforming both SPY and DIA, and NVDA's 5.41% decline is a major drag on the AI-heavy index after Monday's exceptional rally. AP characterized the opening move as a tech-led selloff, while the stronger-than-prior 92.25 consumer-confidence reading does little to ease pressure from the 4.91% Treasury yield. ([apnews.com)

Nvidia is giving back part of a roughly 31% Monday surge tied to the CEO-return news, a setup consistent with profit-taking rather than a fresh upside catalyst. The stock is already trading close to its intraday low and may bounce, but unresolved governance and regulatory concerns cited in morning coverage should keep closing pressure biased downward. (investing.com)

DIA is up 0.42% while QQQ is down 1.36%, indicating active rotation toward less AI-sensitive large caps.
